question: Two trains having lengths of 410 m and 440 m are running at speeds of 60 km/h and 70 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = Sum of train lengths = 410 + 440 = 850 m.

Relative speed (same direction) = 70 − 60 = 10 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/s = 10 × (5/18) = 50/18 m/s.

Time in seconds = Distance ÷ Speed = 850 ÷ (50/18) = 850 × (18/50) = 306 seconds.

Time in minutes = 306 ÷ 60 = 5.1 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.1 minutes.**
